item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03465","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final average 13 after a correct averaging formula; the average is 9.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final count 30 after the correct expression (32 + 13 + 15) − 20; the result is 40.","reason":"Both supply incorrect final numbers after correct formulas, without showing an erroneous calculation.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J03466","case1_error":"Gives unsupported total $475 after correct cost formulas; the equipment costs $752.","case2_error":"Reports the brother’s 11 cars as the three-person total, omitting Tommy’s and Jessie’s six cars.","reason":"The first supplies an unsupported number after correct formulas; the second answers with an intermediate quantity instead of the requested total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03467","case1_error":"Counts only two houses under its equal-area assumption, omitting Zion’s house from the three-person total.","case2_error":"Treats 10 hours over five days as 10 hours per day, inflating the reading rate fivefold.","reason":"The first omits a participant from the total; the second mistakes a multiday amount for a daily rate.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03468","case1_error":"Counts the seven brownies given to friends as brownies remaining, instead of subtracting them from ten.","case2_error":"Counts Sarah’s three donated cupcakes as retained cupcakes when adding the five received cookies.","reason":"Both confuse desserts given away with desserts retained when calculating final holdings.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J03469","case1_error":"Omits the required $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 1/4 × 3 × 14 as 14 rather than 10.5.","reason":"The first leaves a required charge out of its relation; the second numerically miscalculates a correctly written expression.","judgment":"different"}]}
